periods.name: Pre-Historic
periods.description: The earliest period of Indian civilization, marked by cave paintings, rock shelters, and primitive tools. The Bhimbetka rock shelters in Madhya Pradesh contain some of the oldest known rock art in India.

highlights.name: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters
highlights.description: UNESCO World Heritage site with prehistoric rock paintings dating back 30,000 years

periods.name: Proto-Historic
periods.description: The age of the Indus Valley Civilization, one of the world's earliest urban cultures. Cities like Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, and Dholavira showcased remarkable urban planning, drainage systems, and standardized weights.

highlights.name: Dholavira
highlights.description: One of the five largest Harappan sites, known for its sophisticated water management system

highlights.name: Rakhigarhi
highlights.description: Largest Indus Valley Civilization site in India

periods.name: Ancient
periods.description: The golden age of Indian civilization - the era of Mauryas, Guptas, and the birth of Buddhism and Jainism. This period saw the construction of the great stupas, the Ashoka pillars, and the caves of Ajanta.

highlights.name: Lion Capital of Ashoka
highlights.description: The national emblem of India, originally placed atop an Ashoka Pillar

highlights.name: Deogarh Dashavatara Temple
highlights.description: One of the earliest Hindu stone temples with remarkable Gupta-era sculptures

periods.name: Early Medieval
periods.description: The age of regional kingdoms - Cholas, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas, and Rajputs. This period saw the construction of magnificent temples like Brihadeeswarar, Khajuraho, and the Sun Temple at Konark.

highlights.name: Ellora Caves
highlights.description: Rock-cut caves with Hindu, Buddhist and Jain monuments including the incredible Kailasa Temple

highlights.name: Qutub Minar
highlights.description: The tallest brick minaret in the world, begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak

highlights.name: Maitreya Buddha
highlights.description: The 15-meter high statue of Maitreya Buddha at Thiksey Monastery

periods.name: Medieval
periods.description: The Mughal era - a period of architectural magnificence and cultural synthesis. The Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and countless miniature paintings were created during this period.

highlights.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
highlights.description: UNESCO World Heritage baroque church containing the remains of St. Francis Xavier

highlights.name: Meenakshi Temple
highlights.description: Dravidian masterpiece with 14 colorful gopurams and thousands of sculptures

highlights.name: Bundi Miniature Paintings
highlights.description: A distinct school of Rajasthani miniature painting known for its turquoise backgrounds

periods.name: Modern
periods.description: The colonial period and post-independence era. This period saw the Bengal Renaissance, the freedom struggle, and the building of new institutions and monuments like Victoria Memorial and India Gate.

highlights.name: Victoria Memorial
highlights.description: A grand marble building dedicated to Queen Victoria, now a museum

highlights.name: India Gate
highlights.description: War memorial honoring Indian soldiers who died in World War I

periods.name: Contemporary
periods.description: Modern India continues its rich artistic traditions while embracing contemporary forms. Living art forms, traditional crafts, and classical performing arts flourish alongside modern expressions.

highlights.name: Lotus Temple
highlights.description: Bahá'í House of Worship designed in the shape of a lotus flower

highlights.name: Manipuri Dance
highlights.description: One of the major classical dance forms of India, known for its graceful movements
